title: Letter IV
focus: the meeting of two ambitious men

teacherSummary.text: Trapped in ice, Walton's crew sees a giant figure on a dog sled, and the next morning rescues a frozen, exhausted stranger: Victor Frankenstein. Victor recovers slowly, becomes Walton's friend, and, hearing of Walton's ambition, agrees to tell his own story as a warning.

segments.script: The frame (Walton) now opens into Victor's narrative, a 'story within a story' structure called a nested or frame narrative. Victor's warning, 'Learn from me,' makes the whole novel a cautionary tale addressed to Walton and to the reader. Structure: Letter IV turns the frame: Walton meets Victor and becomes the listener. From here the story nests: Walton tells Victor's story, which will contain the creature's. Characterization: Victor appears ruined but eloquent; Walton instantly loves him. Watch Victor's warning speech, which is a teacher's speech. Imagery: The first glimpse is of a "being which had the shape of a man, but apparently of gigantic stature" on a dog-sledge: we see the creature before we know him. Watch for light and fire: Light stands for knowledge and fire for its double edge: warmth and burning. Victor seeks the "light" of discovery; the creature discovers fire and is burned by it. In this chapter: “In the morning, however, as soon as it was light, I went upon deck, and found all the sailors busy on” (Letter IV, paragraph 6).

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “a being which had the shape of a man, but apparently of gigantic stature” slowly and put it in my own words: Walton's crew see a huge figure shaped like a man driving a dog sledge across the ice. Next, craft. I notice the cautious wording, "had the shape of a man, but apparently of gigantic stature," which keeps the figure uncertain. The strongest word is “gigantic”: it marks the being as human in shape but beyond human in size. Then, effect. What do the sailors see on the ice, and why does it matter? My answer: The sailors see a gigantic figure on a dog sledge crossing the ice; it matters because this first sight of the creature makes him a mystery and brings Victor's story to Walton's ship.
